Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account. With me is Daniel, our SE. today we'll walk through Hosted API basics for chat and text — streaming, params, and retry behavior, and we'll show the console quick demo.
[00:11] Ari Patel: Hey Maya, thanks. Quick context: we run internal triage chat for clinicians, low latency requirements, and we currently fan out to a mix of in-house models and OpenAI for fallback. Primary concerns are latency, cost, and PHI handling.
[00:26] Maya Chen: Got it. We'll flag security bits as we go. Daniel, want to kick off with the API surface?
[00:31] Daniel Ruiz: Sure. So the Hosted API is a REST + SDK surface, same endpoints for text and chat. request payload includes model, input or messages, and params like temperature, max_tokens, top_p, and stop sequences. 
[00:45] Daniel Ruiz: For streaming, we support chunked server-sent event style streaming over the same endpoint. You can stream token-by-token or chunked partials, and we expose the SSE events in our SDKs so you can render partial responses quickly.
[00:56] Leah Gomez: How fast is the streaming path? like latency to first token?
[01:01] Daniel Ruiz: Typical p95 to first token for the models we demo on Hosted is in the 150-400ms range depending on model size and prompt length. for shorter prompts you should see under 200ms often. but depends on network, your routing, etc.
[01:13] Jonas Reed: Are those numbers for Redwood hosted multi-tenant? or Dedicated?
[01:17] Daniel Ruiz: That's hosted multi-tenant numbers; Dedicated can be lower and more predictable since you get reserved GPU pools. We can share our model perf spreadsheet later.
[01:25] Maya Chen: Important to note we also do automatic prefix caching for repeated prompts, which can drop cost and latency for conversational flows.
[01:32] Ari Patel: That caching — is it enabled by default on Hosted? and how do we control caching keys?
[01:36] Daniel Ruiz: It's opt-in per-route in the Console. you can set prefix cache TTL and keying strategy; by default it keys on conversation id + recent prompt tokens. we'll send the docs.
[01:47] Mina Park: If we use PHI, what's the retention policy for Hosted? do you allow no-retention or is that only Dedicated/Private?
[01:54] Maya Chen: Hosted API retains transcripts for 30 days by default for analytics but we have an enterprise option for no retention and enterprise contracts often use Dedicated or Private for strict no-retention + customer-managed KMS. I'll put the security pack in the follow-up.
[02:06] Jonas Reed: We need SOC2 and KMS details.
[02:08] Maya Chen: Yep, Jonas — we'll include SOC 2 attestation, KMS integration docs, and the data flow diagram.
[02:14] Daniel Ruiz: Back to streaming: client-side retries and server-side retries — we recommend idempotency keys for request retries on non-streaming requests. On streaming, we provide a resume token option for some models so the client can request continuation if the stream was interrupted; otherwise, fallback to restarting the prompt with dedup checks.
[02:33] Leah Gomez: Resume tokens — is that available across models?
[02:36] Daniel Ruiz: It's model-dependent; for most of our modern chat models we include a resumable stream. we'll check compatibility matrix in the doc we send.
[02:44] Ari Patel: For our triage chat, we expect a lot of short interactions — like 20-80 tokens per turn. What's the recommended param defaults?
[02:52] Daniel Ruiz: For short turns we suggest temperature 0.0-0.3 for deterministic answers, max_tokens tuned to expected reply length, and set top_p to 0.95 or leave default. also set short timeout windows on the client to surface partial answers. batching isn't super useful for single-turn low-latency cases, but our auto-batching can still help throughput at high QPS.
[03:13] Mina Park: What about retry/backoff strategy? we want to avoid duplicate actions in downstream systems when a user submits twice.
[03:18] Daniel Ruiz: Good point — use idempotency keys and dedupe at the application layer. we recommend exponential backoff with jitter and a max of 3 retries for transient 5xx errors; for 429 there's a Retry-After header and we backoff accordingly. for streaming interruptions, try resume token, then full re-try if resume fails.
[03:36] Ari Patel: Can we get a sample snippet for streaming in Python?
[03:39] Daniel Ruiz: yeah — we'll include a sample. (paraphrasing) example: open a streaming client, yield on sse events, render token chunks to UI, and on connection close check resume token to continue. we'll paste the actual code in the follow-up repo link.
[03:53] Leah Gomez: Are there SDKs for Node + Python + Go?
[03:56] Maya Chen: Yes, official SDKs for Python and Node, community Go SDK and some internal examples.
[04:01] Jonas Reed: What's the model catalog like? can we pin to an older version?
[04:04] Daniel Ruiz: You can pin model versions. our catalog lists models with performance profiles and quantization variants. pinning is supported via model version in the request.
[04:12] Ari Patel: Price sensitivity: any rough hosted cost numbers for a 20-token response at our expected QPS?
[04:18] Maya Chen: We'll send an estimated cost calc in the pricing sheet. Hosted cost varies by model; we can also propose a Dedicated pilot if cost predictability is a higher priority.
[04:26] Mina Park: show us the Console streaming demo?
[04:28] Daniel Ruiz: Sure — switching to the Console. (short screen pause)
[04:35] Daniel Ruiz: Here in Console you can create a route, set model, enable streaming checkbox, tune params, and enable prefix caching. I'm simulating a chat — notice how partial tokens stream into the UI. (small audio)
[04:51] Leah Gomez: The live latency overlay is helpful, is that available per-route?
[04:55] Daniel Ruiz: Yeah you get per-route p50/p95, token breakdown, and cost per request estimates.
[05:02] Ari Patel: For PII filtering, do you provide built-in redaction?
[05:06] Maya Chen: We offer a PII detection plugin and you can run redaction pre- or post-inference in your app. again for strict compliance many customers choose Dedicated/Private.
[05:16] Jonas Reed: On Dedicated, can you run in our VPC with customer-managed keys?
[05:19] Daniel Ruiz: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private supports full customer-managed control plane + on-prem options. KMS integration is standard for Enterprise.
[05:28] Ari Patel: Ok, what's the typical POC scope/time to run a bounded pilot?
[05:32] Maya Chen: Typical POC is 2-4 weeks: integration + synthetic benchmark, then small user trial. if you want Dedicated pilot it adds time for infra setup, usually 4-6 weeks.
[05:41] Mina Park: We need to loop in infra and security — Jonas will own that.
[05:45] Jonas Reed: Yep I'll send our security checklist.
[05:47] Maya Chen: Great. quick note on retries and cost — if you do aggressive retries you can spike cost, so we recommend instrumenting request costs in your app and implementing backpressure. Console has route-level quotas and rate-limits too.
[06:02] Daniel Ruiz: One more thing — model fallbacks. you can set a routing policy to fall back to a cheaper model when the primary model is saturated. that helps keep availability up while controlling unit costs.
[06:14] Ari Patel: that seems useful for triage flows.
[06:16] Leah Gomez: Any gotchas with streaming + function calling?
[06:20] Daniel Ruiz: With function/tool calling we stream until the model emits the function call token; then you can either buffer the function args or stream them as they're produced. function calls are supported in streaming but ensure your client handles partial JSON and finalization.
[06:36] Ari Patel: ok good. last — will you share a benchmark script so we can test first token latency from our infra?
[06:42] Daniel Ruiz: yes, we'll send a lightweight script hitting the same endpoints from your region; it supports both streaming and non-streaming tests.
[06:49] (brief cross-talk about calendar invites)
[06:54] Maya Chen: Recap / next steps: 1) Maya sends pricing + no-retention and SOC2 docs; 2) Daniel sends streaming SDK snippet, resume token docs, and benchmark script; 3) Jonas to share security checklist; 4) schedule a POC scoping call w/ infra and security — propose 2026-06-22. any other asks?
[07:12] Ari Patel: that covers it. thanks Maya and Daniel.
[07:15] Maya Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links.
